purpose: Closed-routes map with scope limits for the 2026-10-31 ECDLP index-calculus mega pass. One item per treatise-level closure (brief §2 / treatise chapters), per closed_*/exhausted_at_scale lead in the atlas, and per known-results row in the index-calculus frontier map. 'scope_limits' states the hypotheses the closure needs and the settings where it does NOT apply.
rules: No security claim is made or withdrawn. Measured closures are toy-scale unless stated. 'closed_known' means the mechanism is literature, not that it is impossible. Superseded KR rows are kept with their successor named.
sources: brief/treatise/falldegree.tex (sec:fd-summary, Prop bridges/cert, Thm pkm, tab fd-other)

items.name: Generic oracle bound (Shoup / Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan) on decomposition oracles
items.statement: Any decomposition oracle that decides 'is R an m-sum of base points' by group operations plus membership tests (tables, MITM, enumeration, root tables, subtraction) makes index calculus a generic-group algorithm with advice: T >= sqrt(r/|Aut|) (Shoup) and S*T^2 >~ r/|Aut| (CGK). All compact-orbit k-sum pipelines measured sit 2^25-2^27 above that line; balanced generic IC costs ~r^{2/3}/n^{4/3}.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: oracle uses only group operations and equality/membership tests on group elements; prime-order subgroup; |Aut| counted. DOES NOT APPLY to oracles that read the FIELD REPRESENTATION of coordinates non-generically (Weil descent to F_2-subspaces, Coppersmith on integer lifts of x, bit-level/digit structure, algebraic membership of degree << |F|). The 2^25-2^27 figure is measured only on Koblitz rungs n=61-83; the r^{2/3} formula is a two-term cost model, not a theorem.
items.source: BRIEF §2 row 1; obstructions.tex §'Oracle-augmented index calculus stays generic'; RESEARCH_IC_LEADS_AND_CONNECTIONS_20261010.md §1-2,4
forecloses: online IC after precompute compared against plain rho
items.revisit_when: an oracle that is not GGM-simulable (returns/uses field or curve data, not a group element) with per-query cost polynomial in n at fixed degree

items.name: GGM-simulability of augmented oracles (jet, p-adic lift, endomorphism image, halving, incidence, elliptic net)
items.statement: Jet / p-adic lift oracles (O(1) overhead), endomorphism-image oracles (O(1), scalar on prime-order G), halving queries (equivalent to an x-oracle), factor-base incidence (O(m)) and elliptic-net evaluations (O(log N)) are each simulable in the generic group model, so Shoup's sqrt(r) bound still applies (KN-FIND-002, -b7e091, -194294). Minimal non-simulable order-based identifier is a threshold oracle C_t, which needs private data (KN-FIND-982fdf).
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: oracle is a function of group elements alone (computable from the abstract group with the stated overhead); prime-order subgroup. DOES NOT APPLY to representation-dependent maps (functions of the F_q coordinates that are not group-functorial). Derivation tier, not a measured result; the x-oracle yield measurement (Y_A = Y_B) is toy and marked preliminary (CORR-20261026-c94668).
items.revisit_when: a publicly computable oracle shown NOT GGM-simulable

items.name: Summation-cover monodromy is (Z/2)^{m-2} for every curve; fibres split completely on the factor-base locus; mean yield is a double count
items.statement: For every field K, every E/K and every m>=3: S_m(t_1..t_{m-1},T) is separable of degree 2^{m-2}, its splitting field is K(E^{m-1}/Delta), Galois group (Z/2)^{m-2} acting regularly, arithmetic = geometric monodromy (K algebraically closed in N). Over F_q the fibre splits completely iff all splitting invariants c(a_i) agree, else into 2^{m-3} irreducible quadratics; no factor of degree >=3 ever occurs. On the factor-base locus (a_i = x(P_i), P_i rational) it always splits completely. Mean decompositions per target = C(B+m-1,m)/N for every size-B base (double count). Closes curve selection by monodromy, fibre censuses as relation-rate probes, and 'better geometry raises mean yield'.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: non-degenerate fibre (degenerate locus has O_m(q^{n-1}) points); symmetric base uses the wreath group (Z/2)^{m-2} x| S_{m-1}; conservation needs only a finite abelian group and a fixed base size. LEAVES FREE: coverage (which targets decompose at all, bounded by min(1,mu)), VARIANCE of yield, oracle cost, solving difficulty, linear algebra, where the problem lives. Characteristic-2 separability lemma (E[2] non-reduced) still needs expert check; novelty not adjudicated; full literature search not done. Typed sub-bases are a fixed penalty prod B_i <= (B/m)^m (not an exponent change).
items.source: BRIEF §2 row 3; cover.tex Thm cover/factor/fbsplit, Cor census, Prop conservation; LEAD-ICE-semaev-cover-monodromy (KN-FIND-bdcd60, -4f0d84)
items.revisit_when: a factor-base statistic answering KN-OPEN-62c870 Q1/Q3 that carries curve-specific relation-rate information; rule-12 review breaks the core findings

items.name: Transport conservation under homomorphic transfer (isogenies)
items.statement: A homomorphic transfer phi: E -> E' with rational kernel kappa changes the number of ordered m-decompositions of a target by exactly |kappa|^{m-1} (Lemma conservation). Isogenies buy only kernel symmetry (trivial at prime order), destination factor-base geometry, destination arithmetic cost. Chains compose to one homomorphism; loops are endomorphisms acting as known scalars; multi-curve bases glued by isogenies are single-curve bases in disguise. Measured: fibre-aware IC loses to rho as #E^{1/6} at fixed cofactor.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: transfer is a group homomorphism with rational kernel. DOES NOT COVER non-homomorphic transfers (covers, correspondences, Miller cocycles), which fall under the GHS/cover literature and need an intermediate field or a weak class. The #E^{1/6} loss is measured at fixed cofactor on toy ladders only.
items.revisit_when: a non-homomorphic correspondence with verified scalar compatibility

items.name: No subfield, no low-degree membership (prime p and prime n are one obstruction)
items.statement: Prime p: no subset of F_p of size B has membership degree below B (RESEARCH_PRIME_FIELD_BREAKTHROUGH_PROGRAM §2.3; bounded-degree factor-base theorem IDEA-20260801-021). Prime extension degree n: only F_2 is a proper subfield; no Frobenius-stable F_2-subspace when ord_n(2) = n-1 (n=131, 163); quasi-subfield polynomials closed (beta >= 3/4). Every measured exponent gain (JV cover on F_{p^6}, Gaudry k=3,4, Diem) lives on a field with a proper intermediate subfield.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: membership is an algebraic locus independent of the target; subspace must be Frobenius-stable for the orbit fold. DOES NOT APPLY to non-invariant F_2-subspaces at prime n (Weil descent still works; the cost is the solving degree, open); over F_p the only algebraic handle left is 'x as an integer mod p' (lattices) or digit presentations (open). The prime-field statement is for target-independent algebraic loci; a target-dependent or non-algebraic (e.g. learned, hashed) base is not covered by the degree argument but is covered by the generic bound.
items.revisit_when: KN-OPEN-020 answered positively (size-B set with sub-B-degree membership surviving substitution into S_{m+1})

items.name: Lattice (small-root) reach vs index-calculus demand
items.statement: Jochemsz-May small roots of S_{m+1}: delta_max = 1/(m(m+1)2^{m-2}); needed delta >= 0.169 at m=4 vs reach 0.0125 (13.5x short), 6x short at m=3. Strategy-independent bound: any Coppersmith lattice from (p,f)^t on a convex monomial set has reach <= (n! vol Newt(S_3))^{-1/n} per block = 0.3293 (3 unknowns) / 0.3536 (2 unknowns), attained in 11/11 checks; demand 8/9 at (m,w)=(4,2); for direct S_4/S_5 reach caps at 1/21.8 and 1/70.8 vs targets 1/4 and 1/5. m=2,3 cannot beat sqrt(p) even with a free oracle.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: convex monomial set, lattice of polynomials in (p,f)^t, equal per-variable bounds for the proved part (unequal bounds: numerical only, stops at 1/2), one S_3 block at a time. NOT COVERED: joint three-block lattices for the (4,2) system, non-convex monomial sets, rank-r>=2 GAP substitutions, non-Coppersmith small-root methods, the D4-symmetrised S_5 lattice at m=4 (never run), e-form unequal bounds, multi-ideal lattices. The m=2,3 impossibility is from the two-term cost model with linear algebra included.
items.revisit_when: a joint lattice reaching more than the per-block sum; a non-convex or unequal-bound allocation beating 1/2 per block; a non-Coppersmith small-root solver

items.name: Heights: sums of small points are not small; xedni lift exponent alpha=3
items.statement: Canonical height satisfies h(P+Q)+h(P-Q) = 2h(P)+2h(Q), so a lift of E(F_p) to E(Q)/E(K) has no sub-multiplicative size function and no smoothness notion; this is the common obstruction behind xedni, 'no sub-B membership degree' lifts, and every char-0 lifting idea. On the frozen rational-elliptic-surface family (deg b = 6, monic quadratic x) the exact lift probability is P_lift(p) = (1-2/p+p^{-3})/(2p^3), alpha = 3 (needs alpha < 1/2), checked on 596,268,874 slots, re-derived by parameter count.
items.scope_limits: The alpha=3 result is FAMILY-SPECIFIC: deg b <= 10, deg a <= 4, sections deg x <= 3, p <= 31. A dimension count over ALL section shapes is missing; explicit high-rank K3 fibrations with a dimension surplus are not covered. Height-compressing lifts (CM canonical lifts with cheap field of definition, function-field sections) remain open_next_step in the atlas. The height identity itself is a theorem for any global field.
items.source: BRIEF §2 row 7; obstructions.tex §Lifting sections; RESEARCH_IC_LEADS_AND_CONNECTIONS §7(c); LEAD-ICP-xedni-function-field-sections; EV-XEDN-001
items.revisit_when: a surface family with more free section parameters than prescribed conditions whose measured lift exponent is below 1/2

items.name: Twist points carry no relations
items.statement: A curve and its quadratic twist share x-coordinates and summation polynomials, but Frobenius acts as +1 on E(F_q) and -1 on the embedded twist part, so the twist component B of any mixed sum satisfies 2B = 0: mixed sums are never rational. Checked exactly on toy binary curves in the ECC2K-130 model: 0 of 356,530,036 mixed sums rational, 0 violations on 4,954 targets at m=2,3, predicted off-parity solution sets matched 1,154/1,154; positive controls found all planted solutions.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: odd n, twist a -> a+1 in the binary model (odd characteristic analogue via quadratic character). The obstruction is exact. UNRESOLVED: twist-AVOIDING factor-base subspaces at prime degree. Composite degree N = dn, n >= 3: all-lift F_{2^d}-lines exist when Tr(a)=0 (2^n relations per Gaudry-Diem trial; applies to c2pnb208w1/c2pnb368w1; modelled +0.50 bits, a model output not a measurement). Prime degree: that construction does not exist; all-lift subspaces of dim 4-5 exist at small n (0.921 +- 0.018 of null at N=11, p = 2e-5) but this is toy evidence only; 11 Lean theorems cover the construction, standard axioms.
items.source: BRIEF §2 row 8; obstructions.tex §Twist points carry no relations; research/twist_obstruction_20261026, research/lift_dense_factor_base_20261027
items.revisit_when: useful twist-avoiding subspaces at cryptographic prime degree

items.name: First fall degree is a constant of the presentation; it does not bound the last fall / solving degree
items.statement: In the three presentations studied the first fall degree is a proved constant: 2 for binary Weil descent of S_3, B+1 for explicit membership (guarded chain), 4 for prime Kummer towers (t>=2, g != 0, 3x_R^2+a != 0, inconsistent system). The last fall degree is NOT bounded by it: proved for the guarded chain at B=3 (d_F = 5 vs 4), certified d_F >= 5 vs 2 on named binary instances at n=33-45 and the m=t=3 chain, measured 6 vs 4 for Kummer towers at t=10. Dual-certificate Proposition: one accepted certificate for 1 notin W_4(F) proves no F4 run under any selection strategy stays at degree 4. Semaev's Assumption 1 fails as stated. PKM: d_F depends on presentation, not ideal (naive presentation d_F >= 2^t vs tower d_F <= 2t+2). Any complexity argument substituting first fall degree for solving degree is unsupported for these systems.
items.scope_limits: WHAT IS NOT SETTLED: no presentation has a proved last-fall lower bound growing with n (open problem of HKY and Kousidis-Wiemers); upper bounds k+2 and (t-1)k+t are linear in n and far above observed values. Certificates committed only as hashes (regenerable, not publicly hosted); sample small (two instances per n at n>=33, one polynomial instance at n>=41); written proofs need expert review; Kummer-tower raw data never committed (session-reported). Measured D at m=3 fits ceil(l/2)+4, at m=4 fits l+4; cells (m,l)=(4,4),(4,5),(4,6) UNMEASURED; the 106-bit spread between 'levelled at 7' and 'follows l+4' at n=131 is the open security question. Every observed growth is in base size (l, k, t, B, digit count s), none in n at fixed base (measured range n<=63).
items.source: BRIEF §2 row 9; falldegree.tex sec:fd-summary, Prop bridges/cert, Thm pkm, tab fd-other; RESEARCH_IC_LEADS_AND_CONNECTIONS §5; KR-IC-139da0
items.revisit_when: a proved d_F lower bound growing with n (kills subexponential heuristics) or a bound f(m) independent of n (revives them)

items.name: Frontier measurement: no IC below rho on any prime or prime-degree binary curve
items.statement: 4,848 priced executions: no IC arm below rho on any prime-field or prime-degree binary curve at any price weight. Koblitz 4.7-18x rho at 37-47 bits; prime 5.3-102x at 20-40 bits; random binary 10.6-38x. Every online-class win retired by equal-advice Bernstein-Lange audits (53-317x faster online at equal advice; precomputed rho wins every N83 matched pair, 3.74x-396x).
items.scope_limits: A MEASUREMENT at toy sizes (binary n=13-45, Koblitz n=41-83, prime 20-63 bits), not a theorem; extrapolation to n=131 is by fitted exponents (ln(IC/rho) slope 0.165 [0.117,0.213] per ln r on Koblitz). Weak EXTENSION-FIELD families DO cross rho: genus-3 GHS (exponent ~1.356 vs 1.5), plane quartics via Diem (exponent 0.983, 0.005x rho to q~2^22, pending isolated-host validation), Joux-Vitse covers on E(F_{p^6}) (crossover extrapolated near p~1330), k=4 char-2 near m*~17.6 (16.3-19.2). These are known algorithms fairly measured, on undeployed classes. No measured arm has yet been compared against a PUBLISHED index-calculus reference at the same (q,n,m) (open problem 10).
items.source: BRIEF §2 row 10; prog_openproblems.tex items 2,6,8,9,11; LEAD-ICB-generic-table-oracle; LEAD-ICB-retained-setup-online
items.revisit_when: an arm with fitted exponent below 1/2 in r across the whole pricing band

items.name: Wagner / k-list: relation collection is a k-sum problem with no small visible quotient
items.statement: Finding P_1+...+P_k = O over k lists is the generalised birthday problem, but Wagner's 2^{n/3} needs a group homomorphism to a small quotient visible in the representation; E(F_q) has none except E/<G> (the cofactor, 2 bits on ECC2K-130), so sort-and-match at n^4K^4/r is the best generic rate; residual and large-prime walks lose above r^{1/4} bases because there is no quotient to walk in.
items.scope_limits: HYPOTHESES: the filter is group-theoretic (homomorphic, sum-compatible). DOES NOT COVER a NON-GROUP filter correlated with sums (an 'x-functional filter' whose single-bucket gain grows), which is KN-OPEN-91d4f6 and open. Also leaves open a curve with a large smooth cofactor (not the deployed ones).
items.revisit_when: a non-homomorphic sum-compatible filter with more than log2(cofactor) bits

items.name: Symmetry inventory: every symmetry is polynomial in n or constant
items.statement: Negation (÷2 relations, ÷4 LA, ÷sqrt2 rho), Frobenius on subfield curves (÷n, ÷n^2, ÷sqrt n; Faugere-Svartz character blocks 31-128x on rank at n=11-23), CM automorphisms (÷|Aut|; Z/3 grading costs 12-70x on the solve), 2-torsion translation (FGHR: degree 2^{m-1} -> 2^{m-2}, 30-416x measured on the solve), 4-torsion/Klein (not F_q-valued on subspace bases, Q4 saturation 0.99x), S_m (S_3 17 -> <=10 monomials; S_4-S_8 unmeasured), D4 on S_5 (Bezout 4096 -> 512, projected ~630x on C_4, computed on paper, NEVER RUN), horizontal isogenies (nothing at h(O_K)=1). All polynomial in n or constant; the generic lower bound already includes |Aut|.
items.scope_limits: Symmetry cannot change an exponent; it CAN make the decisive solving-degree cells affordable (equivariant F4 on the full barrel system projected 10-300x, enabler for the (4,l) cells). The D4-symmetrised S_5 lattice/solve is the one symmetry item with projected upside and no measurement. S_4-S_8 symmetrisation unmeasured except saturation at m>=5 balanced l. Gains on the solve compound with base folds (combined >= 0.82) so they should be stacked.
items.revisit_when: never as an exponent lever; as an enabler, whenever a solving-degree cell becomes affordable

items.name: Prime digit presentation: d_ff = d_F = 4 + floor(s/2) at m=2 grows with digit count, reproduced by a curve-free null
items.statement: In the base-B digit presentation of prime-field Semaev systems at m=2 the first and last fall degrees coincide at 4 + floor(s/2), growing with the digit count s; a curve-free null reproduces the same law, so the growth is a property of the presentation size, not of the curve. Bounded-D0 cost models for digit presentations price empty matrices (KN-FIND-0618ab refutes the digit cost tables).
items.scope_limits: Measured at m=2 only; m>=3 digit presentations, their staircase and whether d_F stays flat across >=3 field sizes at fixed s are OPEN (LEAD-ICP-digit-presentation-solving-degree, open_next_step; brief §3 item 9). The curve-free null shows the m=2 law carries no curve information; it does not show that no digit presentation can have bounded degree.
items.source: falldegree.tex §Measured solving degrees in other presentations; KR-IC-401ebf internal note KN-FIND-0618ab
items.revisit_when: a digit presentation at m>=3 whose measured solving degree stays flat across >= 3 field sizes

items.name: Linearisation reach at n=131 is 28-31 bits per trial against 84-99 needed
items.statement: Linearisation of the Weil-descended S_{m+1} systems resolves l + b_max ~ 28-31 bits per trial at n=131 against the 84-99 bits a decomposition needs; gap >= 56 bits at every arity (research/linearization_reach_20260930).
items.scope_limits: A reach calculation for plain linearisation (XL at degree of the field equations) only; Gröbner/closure methods at higher degree are governed by the solving degree (open). Scope: binary n=131, F_2-subspace bases.

items.name: Augmented oracles (x-, y-, full-point, halving, endomorphism-image, incidence, jet) and GGM simulability
items.statement: Each named oracle is GGM-simulable (jet, endomorphism O(1); incidence O(m); halving equivalent to x; net O(log N)), so Shoup's bound closes the family at exponent 1/2 (KN-FIND-002, -b7e091, -194294; EV-GGM-001 strong). Measured: the x-oracle gives yield Y_A = Y_B exactly; the m=3 MITM split saving is attributable to the split, not the oracle.
items.scope_limits: Scope: ORACLES computable from group elements, not RESOURCES (field/curve data, IDEA-20260808-ea3b4f). The threshold oracle is the minimal non-simulable identifier but needs private data. x-oracle yield measurement is toy and marked preliminary (CORR-20261026-c94668).
forecloses: x-coordinate oracle meet in the middle
items.revisit_when: a publicly computable oracle that is NOT GGM-simulable

items.statement: Thirteen screening batches returned FINAL_NO_CANDIDATE / NO_ADMISSIBLE_NEXT_MECHANISM over the checked source set (EV-CRYPTO-010..013); the hyperplane-signature zero-minor route is not sub-rho under its own pinned model at d=1 (KN-FIND-3d6f78, replicated).
items.scope_limits: Exhausted at the scale of the RECORDED SOURCE SET with zero-compute admission sheets; explicitly 'not an impossibility result' (EV-CRYPTO-012). No crypto-size run. The screen's own sensitivity audit (could it have admitted a known positive?) is unperformed (IDEA-20260805-9430e9).

items.name: Alternative curve models and point representations (Edwards, Hessian, Montgomery, Kummer, x-only)
items.statement: Model-native PDP solving degree is invariant (d_reg = 2) between Weierstrass Semaev and twisted Edwards at m=2 and m=3, Edwards a constant factor larger (EV-REP-001/002 replicated); the Kummer line is Bezout-optimal among coordinates E -> P^1, capping the model lever by a one-line degree argument. At most constant factors (Hessian <= 2) remain.
items.scope_limits: Measured only at m=2,3 on toy curves; the Bezout-optimality claim is a proposal-level argument (IDEA-20260905-d0fee4), not a refereed theorem. Does not address constant-factor model gains inside an IC engine (those belong to ic-prime). Does not address coordinates to targets other than P^1 (e.g. Kummer surfaces of products) explicitly.
items.revisit_when: a coordinate E -> P^1 with summation-polynomial degree below the Kummer degree

items.name: Additive-character bias of the discrete log on structured factor bases (H-PSEUDO)
items.statement: Character-sum constant vs matched random null at 2^20-2^26: R = C_EC/C_null flat at 1.28-1.34, i.e. the small-x set behaves like a random set up to a constant; all six standard analytic proof routes closed (KN-FIND-e7a3b1); EXP7 Fourier flatness (8-14 bit) found no candidate predicate. By Betti-yield duality (KN-FIND-9d2f56) sub-rho combinatorial IC needs exactly such a bias.
items.scope_limits: Measured only for the SMALL-X set at 2^20-2^26 (toy) and Fourier flatness at 8-14 bits; no proof either way. Not measured: other structured sets, trends beyond 2^30, multiplicative characters, or sets defined by non-coordinate predicates.

Fourier bias of x-coordinate sets in log order
exponential sum cancellation for the elliptic log

items.name: Elliptic nets / elliptic divisibility sequences as a relation or annihilator source
items.statement: Somos identities hold for every k, so net relations encode the group law on one k-fibre and not k; the net oracle is GGM-simulable with O(log N) overhead (KN-FIND-002); Hankel displacement rank of translated x-blocks is tautological, consecutive blocks have linear complexity >= (M-2)/3. Toy p in {101,431,1601}: collision statistics random-oracle-equivalent; charged k-recovery exponent 1.97-2.80 vs BSGS 1.17-1.32, gap growing 24x -> 135x.
items.scope_limits: Toy prime fields only (p <= 1601, n <= 1607). Closed classes: Hankel / translated-block linear annihilators and rank-1 nets. NOT closed: a target-specific NONLINEAR locator outside those classes; rank >= 2 nets with k-specific relations; the NC2 permuted-net asymmetry in EV-NET-001 is unexplained; EDS period-finding mod p proposal unrun.
forecloses: elliptic net relations for discrete log
Somos sequence sieve on net exponents
short annihilator of an elliptic divisibility sequence
items.revisit_when: a target-specific nonlinear locator or a rank>=2 net with k-specific relations

items.name: Prime-to-p jets, canonical/Teichmuller lifts and p-adic formal-group digits
items.statement: For gcd(n,p)=1 the prime-to-p torsion lifts uniquely (finite etale) with zero formal defect and multiplication by l is invertible on every native jet / formal / p-typical target, so every additive order-l image is zero (IDEA-004 gate, independently verified); jet oracles are GGM-simulable O(1). The digit identity d(mS^) = m d(S^) holds only on the HARD global lift (1360/1360), whose cost is the lift itself; the computable Teichmuller contrast reads as chance under a resolution-matched test (power >= 0.90 for a 3x effect); the IDEA-436 valuation profile collapses to the +/- fibre indicator.
items.scope_limits: Ordinary prime-field curves; measured parts at toy primes of 10-14 bits only. Not excluded: a computable NON-homomorphic local section with above-chance scalar information at a resolution detecting a 3x effect; a succinct manipulation of the hard lift T^ = mS^ without its coordinates (RQ-ECDLP-c1b7b1). Supersingular / p | #E cases not treated here (anomalous case is LEAD-TRF-anomalous-padic-lift).
forecloses: dual-number lift of the addition law
extend Smart anomalous attack to ordinary curves
items.revisit_when: a computable non-homomorphic local section with above-chance scalar information, or succinct manipulation of the hard lift

items.name: Split-Jacobian projected smoothness and the pair (P,Q) as a genus-2 divisor
items.statement: Cross-genus Poincare-factor embedding cannot beat rho on the embedded elliptic factor: the Hasse-Weil order inflation of the ambient Jacobian (#Jac = N * #A, #A = Theta(N^{g-1})) outweighs genus-2 IC savings (KN-FIND-61347e); the projected-smoothness counting gate finds no route with lambda, mu <= 0.45 and its endpoint fails the known-log interface.
items.scope_limits: Same-field embeddings with inflated ambient group order. NOT excluded: a same-field embedding whose ambient group order is O(N) rather than inflated, or a projection with a known-log interface. The (P,Q)-as-one-Mumford-divisor proposal recorded only Stage-0 identities (never run). Extension-field sources are separate leads.

items.name: Torsor, deck-orbit, cubical/biextension and scalar-orbit elliptic-period descent
items.statement: For a generically Galois cover every rational deck-invariant factors through the quotient; a transitive fibre-orbit label is base data; a connected nontrivial cover has no rational section, so a rational target-compatible selector is a missing section/trivialization (IDEA-010 gate, independently verified). The cubical/biextension lift lands on the invertible side of the recognizable/invertible duality: computing its label costs the log.
items.scope_limits: Galois covers and torsors over E with rational labels. NOT excluded: a NON-Galois cover escaping the quotient argument, or a rational target-compatible section of a nontrivial cover. The scalar-orbit elliptic-period idea (IDEA-011) was proposed and never run; closure of it is by the same gate, not by measurement.
forecloses: cubical lift of the prime-order subgroup

items.statement: For E/F_q over F_{q^n} the base {x(P) in V} is pi-stable iff V is sigma-stable; stable subspaces form an arithmetic lattice fixed by the factorisation of X^n-1 over F_q; the gain is exactly n on relations (n^2 on LA) and never more (H-FROB-6774fb; tau pilot: per-attempt decomposition probability at matched |FB| equals the birthday value, n=11..23). At prime n with ord_n(2)=n-1 (131,163) usable stable dimensions are empty. Rho gets the matching sqrt(2n). items.statement: Decomposing into n-1 points over F_{q^n} costs ~(n-1)! q^2 poly((n-1)! 2^{(n-1)(n-2)} log q), beating rho only for n >= 5; the same technique solves oracle-assisted static DH on a 130-bit E(F_{p^5}) faster than generic DLP; Granger analyses static DH over extension fields.

items.name: Modern Gröbner-basis complexity refinements
items.statement: Kudo-Yokoyama 2024 refine degree-of-regularity / solving-degree predictions for affine semi-regular sequences; Jaques-Ran-Samardjiska-Seitner 2026 smooth the degree-of-regularity estimate; Sakata-Takagi efficient MQ F4 variants; Demin 2026 Las Vegas F4 with a proven probability bound.

Semi-regular predictions do NOT describe descended summation systems (KR-IC-58213c), so these refinements bound neither the Weil-descent solving degree nor the IC exponent; they foreclose only re-deriving probabilistic/Las Vegas F4 as novelty. Abstract-level sources.

items.name: First fall degree 2 for the S_3 Weil descent: reported trace mechanism vs a reviewed finite counterexample
items.statement: Abstract/secondary sources report first fall degree 2 for the F_2 Weil descent of S_3 on ordinary binary curves via the trace of x (a group morphism E -> F_2 giving a linear polynomial), and first fall degree of Weil descents bounded independently of n under Hodges-Petit-Schlather conditions. The programme's reviewed finite Boolean control (F_2[t]/(t^4+t+1), n=n'=4, x_R=1, basis [9,3,2,12]) finds no new class at degree 2 and one at degree 3 under its row-space definition; the Lean theorem cited proves only a trace-cancellation identity. Either way the heuristic tying first fall degree to degree of regularity is unsafe for these systems.
items.scope_limits: DISPUTED: whether the sources' definition of first fall degree or their hypotheses exclude the n=4 instance has not been checked against the full texts. Settled regardless: first fall degree (2 or 3) does not bound the solving degree (treatise proves d_ff=2 and certifies d_F>=5). Binary setting only. Supersedes KR-IC-f5c584.
forecloses: low first fall degree of Weil descent

items.name: Characteristic-2 summation algorithms stay far slower than rho
items.statement: Galbraith-Gebregiyorgis (2-torsion and halving symmetries, Gröbner and SAT) and Shantz-Teske conclude that summation-polynomial decomposition on prime-degree binary curves of reasonable size is much slower than rho; experiments reach only small n and l. Programme extensions: descended ANF exceeds the whole rho budget for n <= ~283; ECC2K-130 free oracle at m=3 costs 2^68.58 vs rho 2^60.81.
items.scope_limits: A MEASURED negative at small n, l (literature) plus cost-model extrapolations (programme); abstract-level sources. Not a proof; the open question is the solving-degree growth (brief §3 item 1). Prime-degree binary only.
forecloses: summation polynomial attack on binary curves beats rho

items.name: Naive Semaev index calculus over prime fields cannot beat generic methods
items.statement: Yokoyama-Yasuda-Takahashi-Kogure show, under stated statistical assumptions (a heuristic, not an unconditional proof), that Semaev's naive IC over F_p costs at least as much as generic algorithms; algebraic factor bases (Petit-Kosters-Messeng; Amadori-Pintore-Sala; Kudo et al.) reported to work only at small parameters; McGuire-Mueller's Gröbner-free variant reported still worse than rho. Internal: digit-presentation cost tables refuted; bounded-D0 models price empty matrices.
items.scope_limits: HEURISTIC (statistical assumptions); ALL sources read in abstract only; 'naive' = x-coordinate interval/random base with Gröbner solving. Does not bound a non-naive prime-field IC with a genuinely new oracle (small-root, digit presentation at m>=3, invertible hint subsets). Supersedes KR-IC-5931ee (which had status 'proven' — corrected to heuristic).
forecloses: index calculus over prime field curves
small x-coordinate factor base over F_p

items.name: Gaudry: decomposition over E(F_{q^n}), n fixed
items.statement: For fixed n, Gaudry's decomposition IC on E(F_{q^n}) runs in O~(q^{2-2/n}) (constant ~ n! 2^{n(n-1)}), beating rho's q^{n/2} for n >= 3 asymptotically; F_{q^3}: O(q^{10/7}), F_{q^4}: O(q^{14/9}) with double large primes.
items.scope_limits: FIXED small n, EXTENSION fields with a proper subfield; heuristic; constants enormous in n. Does not apply to prime fields (n=1) or prime n with no intermediate field (the subfield condition x in F_q is what makes membership low-degree). Abstract-level sources.
forecloses: index calculus on curves over small degree extension fields

items.name: Quasi-subfield polynomials
items.statement: IC over binary (and other) fields could be improved if quasi-subfield polynomials X^{p^{n'}} - lambda(X) with small lambda split completely often enough (HKPYY 2020); Euler-Petit prove beta >= 3/4 for linearised complete splitters; existence of useful families remains open. Internal: beta > 1/2 for every complete splitter with n' not dividing n (possibly novel).
items.scope_limits: The bound beta >= 3/4 is for LINEARISED complete splitters; the HKPYY improvement itself is CONJECTURED; existence of useful (non-linearised) families is OPEN in the literature (KN-OPEN-ac409f). Programme closure at n=131 is under the HKPYY cost model.
forecloses: subfield-like factor base for prime degree extensions

items.name: SAT and XOR reasoning for point decomposition
items.statement: SAT solvers (CryptoMiniSat) and XOR-aware WDSat solve binary-curve PDP instances faster than Magma F4 (up to 300x on the PDP step, Trimoska-Ionica-Dequen 2020) without changing the exponent relative to rho. Internal: WDSat's advantage on the authors' instances comes from static branching order; XOR-GE 4-7x slower.
items.scope_limits: Binary PDP, measured constant-factor mechanism. Forecloses SAT/XOR as NOVELTY; does not bound a solver with sub-enumeration UNSAT growth (LEAD-ICB-decomposition-encoding-and-sat measures alpha ~ m for all tried).
forecloses: Gaussian elimination in SAT for PDP

items.name: Last fall degree of zero-dimensional Weil descent systems; solving degree vs last fall degree
items.statement: For a zero-dimensional radical system F over F_{q^n} in m variables with <= s solutions over the closure and an injective coordinate projection, the last fall degree of its Weil descent with field equations is bounded by a function of q, m, s, deg F and the last fall degree of F, independent of n (HKYY Thm 1.1; univariate HKY Main Thm 1, polynomial time in (n+d)^d). Both papers state this does NOT apply to summation-polynomial systems (not zero-dimensional before field equations); whether their last fall degree depends on n is left open. Solving degree = max(last fall degree, max reduced GB degree) for degree-compatible orders (Caminata-Gorla), so a last-fall bound alone does not bound solving degree. Semi-regular predictions do not describe descended summation systems.
items.scope_limits: ZERO-DIMENSIONAL, radical, injective-projection systems only — explicitly NOT summation systems. The n-independence of d_F for summation systems is the open problem (brief §3 item 1). Full-text read. Supersedes KR-IC-fbdb61.
forecloses: last fall degree bounded for zero-dimensional descent systems
semi-regular estimate for summation polynomial systems

items.name: Semaev summation polynomials
items.statement: S_m(x_1..x_m) vanishes exactly when points with those x-coordinates sum to O (with some signs); S_2 = x_1 - x_2, S_3 explicit, S_m = Res_X(S_{m-k+1}, S_{k+1}); degree 2^{m-2} in each variable. Using them to decompose points over a factor base is the IC framework itself. Internal: Galois group (Z/2)^{m-2} and factorization dichotomy (novelty unadjudicated).
items.scope_limits: Framework fact: novelty must lie in representation, factor base, elimination or solver, never in 'use summation polynomials'. Not a closure of any route.
forecloses: decompose a point as a sum of factor base points

items.name: GHS Weil descent and cover attacks
items.statement: GHS Weil descent maps ECDLP on E(F_{q^n}) to a hyperelliptic Jacobian over F_q; effective only for special fields/curves (Menezes-Teske-Weng weak fields; Iijima-Momose-Chao classify vulnerable odd-characteristic curves incl. degree 5); isogenies can move a curve into a vulnerable class (Tian 2023 for some prime-order curves over F_{q^3}).
items.scope_limits: Needs an EXTENSION field with proper subfield (n > 1) and a curve/field in a weak class; prime p and prime n=131 binary are not covered. Forecloses GHS/cover attacks as novelty; abstract-level sources.

items.name: Diem: rigorous subexponential ECDLP for suitable n
items.statement: Diem proves ECDLP on E(F_{q^n}) is subexponential (L(2/3)-type) when n ~ sqrt(log q) (2011) and for n up to about log q (2013). The open cases are prime fields and prime-degree binary fields.
items.scope_limits: Requires n growing with log q (n ~ sqrt(log q) to ~log q) — a family of fields, not a fixed prime field or fixed n=131 over F_2. Rigorous. Explicitly leaves prime fields and prime-degree binary fields open.

items.name: Choosing the factor-base vector space V (small product spaces)
items.statement: In binary PDP the factor base is {P: x(P) in V} for an F_2-subspace V; choosing V so product spaces V^(i) have small dimension (span{1,z,..,z^{l-1}} in polynomial basis, or subfield/linearised structure) lowers degree and variable count after Weil descent (FPPR, Petit-Quisquater, HPST 2013); Shantz-Teske study factor-base choices experimentally.
items.scope_limits: Binary subspace bases; heuristic; forecloses 'choose V to minimise dim V^2' as novelty. The programme measured all such effects as constants vanishing with size (LEAD-ICB-factor-base-subspace-choice). Non-subspace bases not covered.
forecloses: choose V to minimise dim V^2
polynomial basis subspace span 1 z z^2

items.name: Weak binary fields under GHS and generalized GHS with isogeny walks (Menezes-Teske-Weng, Menezes-Teske), exact densities and costs
items.statement: Over F_{2^N}, N = nl composite, N in [160,600]: N = 5l weak (every non-subfield curve magic number 5, genus 15/16 over F_{2^l}; speedup 2^6 at N=185 to 2^69 at N=600 on 2003 timings); N = 210 particularly weak (2^13 all curves, 2^20 for the Tr(a)=Tr(b)=0 quarter via the (6,5) family of density 2^-34 reached by a ~2^34-step walk costing ~2^60 ops); N = 3l partially weak (genus-3 hyperelliptic family, density 2^-(l-1), q/2 walk steps, Gaudry-Thome O(q^{4/3})); N = 6l potentially weak (Hess genus 14 density ~1, genus 12 density 2^-(l-1)); N = 7l, 8l potentially partially weak; N = 4l only slightly weak (genus 8); N prime, and N not divisible by 3,5,6,7,8, NOT weak under either attack. 'Weak' = cheaper than the hardest rho over the same field, time only; no field known to be bad. Subfield curves not weakened (descent kills the large subgroup). c2pnb176w1 best instance (8,5) would cost 2^61-2^65 vs rho 2^87 but has density ~2^-66 in its class (harder to reach than rho).
items.scope_limits: COMPOSITE N only; prime N (all NIST/SEC binary curves, ECC2K-130) explicitly not weak under GHS/gGHS. Hess-family densities rest on Assumptions A, B (non-hyperelliptic Jacobian costs) and C (uniform density across endomorphism classes); n=5 and n=3 results need neither A nor B. Timings are 2003 ratios. Full-text read.

items.name: Subexponential binary ECDLP under the first fall degree assumption
items.statement: Petit-Quisquater (2^{c n^{2/3} log n}, crossover n ~ 2000), FPPR, Semaev 2015 (2^{c sqrt(n ln n)}, claimed below rho for some FIPS curves under Assumption 1, regularity <= 4) and Nagao 2015 (polynomial) all rest on first-fall-degree-type assumptions; HKY, Kosters-Yeo, HPST 2015 and later give evidence the assumption fails; Galbraith-Gaudry record no consensus. Internal: memory-charged crossover vs coherent vOW moves to n = 460/520; Assumption 1 measured on the wrong subspaces, first fall degree flat at 3 on the right ones (n=7..63); Nagao Lemma 4 false over F_2 under the equality reading.
items.scope_limits: DISPUTED claims, not closures: the subexponential claims are unsupported (assumption fails), but their FALSITY is not proved either — no d_F lower bound growing with n exists (KN-OPEN-d218ec, -86e7e1). Even if PQ held, the n ~ 2000 crossover leaves n=131 unaffected. Binary only.

items.name: Point decomposition via symmetric formulations (Karabina)
items.statement: Karabina reformulates binary-curve PDP using symmetric functions and Weil restriction to reduce the system; gain is a constant/polynomial factor in the decomposition step.
items.scope_limits: Binary PDP; constant/polynomial factor only; full-text read. Forecloses symmetric-function reformulation as novelty, not as an engineering lever.

items.name: Symmetries and torsion speed up point decomposition
items.statement: Exploiting S_m symmetry and small-order torsion (twisted Edwards/Jacobi models, 2- and 4-torsion) reduces PDP cost by about 2^{omega(n-1)}; FGHR estimate ~2^130 word ops for twisted Edwards over F_{q^5}, q ~ 2^64 (vs 2^160 generic); symmetrised summation polynomials (FHJRV) use small-order torsion to shrink systems further.
items.scope_limits: EXTENSION fields F_{q^n} with rational small-order torsion; heuristic estimates; constant/polynomial factors. The ecGFp5 (Z/2)^4 x| S_5 quotient-ideal degree is OPEN (KN-OPEN-9b4a2b). Binary prime-degree: 2-torsion gives FGHR constants only (treatise symmetry inventory).

items.name: Survey consensus (2016)
items.statement: Galbraith-Gaudry 2016: no consensus that binary-field ECDLP is subexponential; IC has no practical impact at deployed sizes; prime-field ECDLP has no known attack better than rho for general curves.
items.scope_limits: A 2016 survey statement; abstract/conclusions only. Forecloses nothing mathematically — it is the baseline any novelty claim is measured against.
forecloses: index calculus is practical for deployed curves
prime field ECDLP better than rho

items.name: Hyperelliptic index calculus and the genus threshold
items.statement: For genus g Jacobians over F_q, IC with double large primes costs O~(q^{2-2/g}) (Gaudry-Thome-Theriault-Diem), beating rho's q^{g/2} for g >= 3; decomposition attacks extend to Jacobians over extension fields (Nagao 2010; Tsakou-Ionica with endomorphisms).
items.scope_limits: HYPERELLIPTIC (and via Diem, plane quartic at O~(q)) Jacobians of genus >= 3 over F_q; heuristic. For an elliptic curve this bites only after a transfer into such a Jacobian over a SMALLER field (GHS/cover); same-field embeddings inflate the group (LEAD-TRF-same-field-genus-g-embedding).

items.name: Largest practical algebraic ECDLP computations
items.statement: Cover-and-decomposition IC solved a 149-bit prime-order subgroup of E(F_{p^6}) in ~110,000 CPU-hours (Joux-Vitse 2012); GLS-assisted GHS descent broke a prime-order subgroup over F_{2^{5*31}} in ~1,035 CPU-days (Chi-Dominguez-Rodriguez-Henriquez-Smith 2021). No summation-polynomial method has beaten rho on a cryptographic-size prime-field or prime-degree binary curve.
items.scope_limits: Records on EXTENSION fields with intermediate subfields (p^6, 2^{155}); the negative sentence is a statement about the record books (reported), not a theorem.
forecloses: largest ECDLP solved by index calculus

items.name: Frobenius-invariant factor bases for subfield (Koblitz) curves
items.statement: For subfield curves E/F_q with ECDLP in E(F_{q^n}), Frobenius-invariant factor bases reduce the number of systems to solve by up to 1/n (best possible) and speed linear algebra by n^2 (Galbraith-Granger-Merz-Petit). Internal: p | n cells, exact spectra; at q=2, n in {131,163} the stable subspace is a net loss.
items.scope_limits: Koblitz/subfield curves; polynomial (n, n^2) factor, 'best possible' at 1/n; heuristic; abstract read (re-derived internally). At prime n with ord_n(2) = n-1 (131, 163) no usable stable subspace exists. KN-OPEN-095df5 open.

items.name: Xedni calculus and lifting to characteristic zero fail
items.statement: Silverman's xedni calculus (lift points to Q, look for rank-deficient lifts) was shown by Jacobson-Koblitz-Silverman-Stein-Teske to succeed with negligible probability; lifting-based ECDLP approaches inherit this obstruction. Internal: exact-counting closure of FB-geometry and xedni lifting (GOAL-ICLIFT-001, 2026-07-24).
items.scope_limits: Classical xedni over Q (heights grow; small points reduce uniformly). 'Lifting-based approaches inherit this' is an extrapolation: height-compressing lifts (CM canonical lifts with cheap field of definition; function-field sections with dimension surplus) are open_next_step in the atlas; the function-field alpha=3 result is one frozen family. Abstract-level sources.

items.name: ecGFp5 and degree-5 extension curves: published estimates
items.statement: ecGFp5 over F_{p^5}, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1: designer estimates >= 2^142 for Gaudry-type decomposition and O(C p^2), p^2 = 2^128, for Joux-Vitse; FGHR's ~2^130 for twisted Edwards over F_{q^5} relies on symmetries whose applicability to ecGFp5 is unexamined; no dedicated cryptanalysis found (2026-09-26).
items.scope_limits: Designer ESTIMATES, not measurements; the 2^121 symmetrized-decomposition prediction is unmeasured (EV-GFPN-ba8e4d); the (Z/2)^4 x| S_5 quotient degree is open. These are open leads under GOAL-GFPN-380702, not closures.

items.name: Crossbred algorithm for Boolean systems
items.statement: Joux-Vitse's crossbred combines Macaulay-matrix preprocessing with exhaustive search for Boolean systems and beats both pure approaches in its regime.
items.scope_limits: Generic Boolean systems; forecloses crossbred/hybrid as novelty only. Programme measurement (research/crossbred_20260920): relation collection stays Theta(2^n) with any oracle polynomial in the base.
forecloses: hybrid Macaulay plus enumeration for Boolean systems

items.name: F4 trace reuse across many similar systems
items.statement: Joux-Vitse's F4 variant records the reduction trace of one system and replays it on many similar systems (as in decomposition), avoiding repeated symbolic work. Internal: the 'learn one trace and replay branch-free' GPU premise failed at n=17.
items.scope_limits: Engineering constant; forecloses trace replay as novelty. The programme found replay is not branch-free on descended Semaev systems at n=17 (closure degrees vary per instance).
forecloses: learn one elimination trace and replay branch-free

items.name: The trace morphism forces a linear equation (first fall degree 2 for S_3) (superseded row)
items.statement: Weil descent to F_2 of S_3 on ordinary binary curves has first fall degree 2 because Tr(x): E -> F_2 is a group morphism yielding a linear polynomial after descent; first fall degree of Weil descents bounded independently of n under Hodges-Petit-Schlather conditions.
items.scope_limits: SUPERSEDED by KR-IC-139da0 (status disputed after a reviewed finite counterexample under the row-space definition). Use the successor's scope. The treatise independently PROVES d_ff = 2 for binary S_3 descent in its own presentation (falldegree.tex); the dispute is about definitions/hypotheses, and in all readings d_ff does not bound d_F.

items.statement: Last fall degree of Weil-descended systems is bounded independently of the extension degree under stated conditions (HKY; HKYY); solving degree, last fall degree and degree of regularity are related but distinct (Caminata-Gorla; Caminata-Ceria-Gorla; Semaev-Tenti); semi-regular predictions do not describe descended summation systems.
